This episode of Statecraft examines major global political battles and their geopolitical repercussions. In Israel, following an inconclusive general election where Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc secured 53 seats, the Likud party alleged widespread electoral fraud and foreign interference involving Arab parties, Qatar, and Turkey. Israeli election authorities and police found no evidence of systematic fraud or altered outcomes. Meanwhile, rival opposition factions and Arab parties hold potential kingmaker positions amid tense coalition maneuvers. Across the Atlantic, the upcoming US midterm elections threaten Republican control of Congress, presenting significant implications for India. With bilateral trade negotiations stalled over agriculture and Russian oil imports, shifts on Capitol Hill could reshape US tariff policies, trade scrutiny, and strategic ties. In diplomatic developments, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar arrived in Atlanta for the G20 foreign ministers meeting and Quad deliberations chaired by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, before heading to the Commonwealth summit. The show concludes with scenes of physical brawls erupting inside Armenia's parliament. Read More

Rahul Gandhi vs Nirmala Sitharaman on IDBI Bank Privatisation, PSU Valuation & Tata Group
A major political clash has erupted between Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman over the proposed privatization of IDBI Bank. Rahul Gandhi accused the Narendra Modi government of undervaluing a premier public institution built during the Congress era and questioned the bidding process, also raising concerns regarding employee rights. Hitting back, Nirmala Sitharaman defended the sale, asserting that all prescribed procedures were followed and blaming Congress-era crony lending for burdening IDBI Bank with massive bad loans. The controversy follows previous exchanges between both leaders regarding corporate governance and alleged government interference in the Tata Group. On the broadcast, experts including SBI Group Chief Economic Advisor Soumya Kanti Ghosh, former Finance Secretary S.C. Garg, and political analyst Rajat Sethi debated the bank's turnaround, reserve price revisions, and the valuation benchmark set for the stake sale to Fairfax Financial Holdings. In a subsequent segment, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav outlined anti-pollution measures across Delhi-NCR.
Rain Disrupts INDIA Bloc Event; Gyanesh Kumar Impeachment Postponed, Ramlila Rally On
Rain lashed Delhi, upsetting the INDIA bloc's arrangements to stage a public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's 10 Rajaji Marg residence. The downpour washed away sound and lighting systems on the lawns and drenched tables and tents, leaving the setup covered under waterproof sheets. Following the disruption, Rahul Gandhi addressed a joint press conference alongside allied leaders, announcing that the symbolic event has been delayed by 24 hours to Saturday noon. Leaders stressed that the mass outreach will take place ahead of their scheduled mega Ramlila Maidan march on November 1.

Resignation From Power, J&K Politics and Survival of National Conference
A former three-time Member of the Legislative Assembly in Jammu and Kashmir, who served with the Jammu & Kashmir National Conference for twenty-five years, explains his decision to relinquish power and surrender his legislative seat on principled grounds. Addressing the prevailing political climate, he characterizes his move as a conscious choice driven by conviction rather than political opportunism. He outlines his intention to mobilize trustworthy individuals committed to ethical politics before establishing a formal political alternative, while noting that he may contest an upcoming by-election as an independent candidate. Reflecting on the state of the ruling party, he asserts that the organization has abandoned its core ideology and promises. He further observes that the survival and cohesion of the National Conference remain inextricably tied to the presence of party patriarch Farooq Abdullah, expressing doubt over its long-term viability under its current leadership direction.
